clonable and modifiable. | | architecture_claims | +1 | `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md` corroborates the epic's premise: the Dashboard is the GA single-pane web console that surfaces projects, workbenches, model serving, and pipelines via creation/edit forms — exactly the four audited flows — and is Konflux-onboarded, supporting the CI-green acceptance criterion. | ", "artifacts/epic-tasks/RHAISTRAT-9017-E001.md": "--- epic_id: RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 title: Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows parent_strat: RHAISTRAT-9017 component: Dashboard team: RHOAI Dashboard type: Implementation priority: P1 dependencies: [] ai_signals: change_specificity: 1 pattern_precedent: 1 adapter_pattern: 0 existing_foundation: 1 open_questions: 1 external_dependency: 1 human_process_gates: 1 repo_access: 1 architecture_claims: 1 implementation_type: null investigation_signals: null ai_implementability: High ai_implementability_score: 8 jira_key: «redacted» null gated_by: null gate_failure_impact: null --- # Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows ## Description This epic makes the four audited core Dashboard flows — project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission — fully operable with keyboard alone, and makes visible focus indicators consistent across those flows. It resolves every defect enumerated in the accessibility audit report for these flows: focus loss in modals, controls unreachable via keyboard, and inconsistent focus indicators. ## Scope - Remediate each defect enumerated in the accessibility audit report across the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission): - Fix focus handling in modals so focus is not lost — focus enters the modal when it opens, remains trapped within it while it is open in the tab order, and returns to the triggering control when it closes. - Make every interactive control in the audited flows reachable and operable via keyboard (tab order, arrow-key navigation where the control type expects it, Enter/Space activation, Escape to dismiss). - Apply a single consistent visible focus-indicator treatment across all interactive controls in the audited flows, replacing the current inconsistent indicator styles. - Out of scope per the strategy: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require, and any flows outside the four audited ones. Any audited defect whose resolution would require out-of-scope semantics is dispositioned with a recorded rationale rather than silently dropped. - The Dashboard's existing build pipeline and CI must remain green with these changes. ## Acceptance Criteria - Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end-to-end using the keyboard alone, verified by a recorded keyboard-only walkthrough of each flow. - Every defect enumerated in the audit report for these flows is resolved, or explicitly dispositioned as out of scope with a recorded rationale. - No focus traps remain: opening and closing any modal in the audited flows moves focus into the modal and returns it to the triggering control. - No unreachable controls remain: every interactive control in the audited flows is reachable via keyboard and operable without a pointing device. - A single focus-indicator treatment is applied consistently across all interactive controls in the audited flows (no per-page or per-flow indicator variations). - The Dashboard's existing build pipeline is green with the changes included. ## HLR Traceability - **HLR-1 (P1)**: The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. - **HLR-2 (P1)**: Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. The published conformance statement is a customer-facing deliverable: two public-sector customers require it before renewal. ## Scope Content outline: - Update the VPAT so its conformance claims for keyboard operability and focus visibility reflect the actual fixed behavior of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission). - Update the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the current accessibility state, including any remaining known limitations outside the four audited flows and outside keyboard scope (screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require are out of scope for the fixes and must be stated accurately as limitations where relevant). - Republish both artifacts through the standard Red Hat documentation content process so the updated conformance statement is publicly available. - Every conformance claim must trace to a verified, shipped fix — no claim may assert behavior beyond what the implementation delivers. ## Acceptance Criteria - The VPAT is updated so that each keyboard-operability and focus-visibility claim accurately reflects the implemented behavior of the four audited flows, with no claim that overstates the shipped state. - The product docs accessibility statement is updated and republished. - Each conformance claim in the updated VPAT traces to a specific verified fix in the audited flows (claim-to-fix traceability recorded). - The updated documentation has been technically reviewed against the implementation (keyboard accessibility remediation of the audited flows) and the review sign-off is recorded before republication. ## HLR Traceability - **HLR-3 (P2)**: The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. No replacement epics exist, so no rollback/ feature-flag AC is required. No AC is an externally-controlled precondition (the review sign-off is the rule-mandated docs-authoring gate, not a misfiled risk note). No draft-ID references to sibling epics appear in either epic body. ### 7. Completeness (2/2) All strategy scope is covered: the four audited flows' keyboard operability and focus-indicator consistency (E001), and the VPAT + accessibility statement update, technical review, and republication (E002). The customer-renewal context is carried into E002's description; the audit-report external input is carried into E001's scope with an explicit disposition-not-drop rule for out-of-scope semantics, and E002's scope requires remaining limitations to be stated accurately. Can the strategy deliver partial value without it?\n153\t2. **YES** → Split into:\n154\t - **Tier 1**: Independent work (user-facing features OR risk-reduction spikes/validations)\n155\t - **Tier 2**: Dependency-gated work (blocked by upstream epic)\n156\t3. **NO** → Linear dependencies; external dependency blocks all downstream\n157\t\n158\t## Step 6: Classify Epics\n159\t\n160\tFor each epic, determine:\n161\t\n162\t### Type (mandatory)\n163\t- **Implementation**: Produce an artifact (code, config, docs, manifests, pipelines, RFCs, upstream PRs)\n164\t- **Investigation**: Resolve uncertainty (answer a question or make a decision that other epics depend on)\n165\t\n166\t### Implementation Type (optional routing label)\n167\t\n168\t| Label | When to apply |\n169\t|-------|--------------|\n170\t| `docs-authoring` | Red Hat docs content process — specialized tooling |\n171\t| `konflux-onboarding` | Build pipeline onboarding — known-recipe |\n172\t| `license-validation` | License scanning for transitive dependencies |\n173\t| `repo-onboarding` | Midstream repo fork creation under opendatahub-io |\n174\t| _(absent/null)_ | General-purpose — read target repo, figure it out |\n175\t\n176\t### AI Implementability Signals\n177\t\n178\tScore signals so the pipeline can compute an AI-implementability classification deterministically. **Do not compute the total score or classification yourself.** Use the signal set that matches the epic `type` — Implementation and Investigation epics measure different things.\n179\t\n180\t#### Implementation epics → `ai_signals` (9 signals)\n181\t\n182\tEvaluate each as +1 (favorable), 0 (neutral/N/A), or -1 (unfavorable). Write the values into `ai_signals`.\n183\t\n184\t| # | Signal | Frontmatter key | +1 Condition | -1 Condition |\n185\t|---|--------|----------------|-------------|-------------|\n186\t| 1 | Change specificity | `change_specificity` | Exact file paths, API endpoints, field names known | Vague scope (\"improve X\") |\n187\t| 2 | Pattern precedent | `pattern_precedent` | Similar changes exist in same codebase | No precedent in codebase |\n188\t| 3 | Adapter/plugin pattern | `adapter_pattern` | Follows existing reference implementation | N/A (0 if absent) |\n189\t| 4 | Existing foundation | `existing_foundation` | Extending existing code/feature | Greenfield, no foundation |\n190\t| 5 | Open questions | `open_questions` | All design decisions resolved for this epic | Open questions that would change implementation approach |\n191\t| 6 | External dependency | `external_dependency` | None | Upstream contribution or vendor coordination needed |\n192\t| 7 | Human process gates | `human_process_gates` | None | Requires human approval step |\n193\t| 8 | Repo access | `repo_access` | AI can clone and modify target repo | Repo inaccessible or special access required |\n194\t| 9 | Architecture claims | `architecture_claims` | Epic's scope or the strategy's premise about the component (surfaces, repos, deployment model, maturity state such as Tech Preview/GA) is corroborated by an architecture-context file — name that file in the rationale | Strategy asserts architecture that the context files contradict or cannot back |\n195\t\n196\t**Scoring `architecture_claims` (signal 9):** a strategy makes architecture claims whenever it states what a component IS — its maturity state (\"shipped as Tech Preview\", \"generally available\"), its CRD/API/repo surfaces, its deployment model — even when it never uses the word \"claim\". If the strategy indicates the resolution could require a different approach (conditional ADRs, \"if X requires changes to Y\"), evaluate which downstream epics build on the current assumption and gate them on the resolution.\n230\t\n231\t## Step 7: Derive Acceptance Criteria\n232\t\n233\tEach epic gets acceptance criteria derived from:\n234\t- Strategy acceptance criteria allocated to this epic's scope\n235\t- HLRs mapped to this epic\n236\t- Implementation-specific requirements (build pipeline green, rollback plan, doc review, etc.)\n237\t- Rules 23-25 from Step 5\n238\t\n239\tEvery AC must be a testable pass/fail condition on THIS epic's own deliverable — something the epic's engineering work produces or verifies. Set frontmatter via script:\n258\t\n259\t```bash\n260\tpython3 scripts/frontmatter.py set artifacts/epic-tasks/{ID}-decomposition.md \\\n261\t parent_strat=\"{ID}\" epic_count= critical_path_length=\n262\t```\n263\t\n264\tAdd `triage= triage_rationale=\"\"` for triaged strategies (Step 0).\n265\t\n266\t### Scope constraint: decompose, don't design\n267\t\n268\tYour job is to break strategy scope into units of work, not to make implementation decisions.\n269\tIf the strategy describes a capability at a functional level, the epic scope stays at that level.\n270\tDo not invent API paths, URL schemas, response formats, environment variables, caching policies,\n271\tCRD field names, or other implementation details not stated in the strategy. Do not set it earlier: anything you write or edit after setting it may be reviewed in a partially written state.\n353\t\n354\t### Conditional decomposition (when applicable)\n355\t\n356\tIf an Investigation epic has ≤3 bounded outcomes that change downstream structure, write one file per branch epic using the `-BRANCH--` filename convention:\n357\t\n358\t```\n359\t{ID}-E001.md # Shared epic (the Investigation that selects the branch)\n360\t{ID}-BRANCH-A-E003.md # If outcome A\n361\t{ID}-BRANCH-B-E003.md # If outcome B\n362\t{ID}-BRANCH-B-E004.md # Extra epic in branch B\n363\t```\n364\t\n365\t**Branch epics are not standalone Jira issues.** The pipeline attaches each branch's epics to the gating Investigation epic as a plan document; it does not create them as issues or wire Blocks links from them.
